\newcommand{\SIR}{\operatorname{S-I-R}}

# Set up details and utilities
Load required modules.
Note that `EpidemicsCFTP` is under development, while `FigureUtilities` needs in due course
to be pre-compiled!
```{julia}
using Colors, Compose, DataFrames, Measures
import Cairo, Fontconfig, Gadfly
gf = Gadfly

using EpidemicsCFTP 

include("./FigureUtilities.jl")
using .FigureUtilities ;
```

Here are some very basic features about the epidemic.
```{julia}
const population = 6 ;
const duration   = 3 ;
const MAXPOP  = 20 ;
if population > MAXPOP
  error("`population` exceeds `$(MAXPOP)`: modify code indexing time-lines!")
end ;
```


# Abbreviations and choices for style and style colour
Set up and establish graphics size and coordinates.
```{julia}
set_default_graphic_size(6inch, 3.25inch) ;
coordinates = UnitBox(0, population, duration, -population,
  leftpad=0.5inch, rightpad=0.5inch, toppad=0.25inch, bottompad=0.3inch) ;
```

Abbreviations for various kinds of incidents.
```{julia}
A = AbstractInfection
R = Removal            ; C = CRemoval   
I = Infection          ; P = PInfection
IR = InitialRemoved    ; II = InitialInfected    ; IS = InitialSusceptible
CR = ContinuingRemoved ; CI = ContinuingInfected ; CS = ContinuingSusceptible
MIA = MarkerInfectionA ; MRA = MarkerRemovalA
MIB = MarkerInfectionB ; MRB = MarkerRemovalB ;
```

Code colours for various kinds of incidents using a function `csty`.
See <https://juliagraphics.github.io/Colors.jl/stable/namedcolors/> for a useful list of colours.
```{julia}
function csty(x::Vector{R}) colorant"tan"       end 
function csty(x::Vector{C}) colorant"purple"    end 
function csty(x::Vector{I}) colorant"orange"    end 
function csty(x::Vector{P}) colorant"darkgreen" end 

function csty(x::Vector{T}) where T<:AbstractInfection         colorant"yellow" end 
function csty(x::Vector{T}) where T<:AbstractInfectionMarker   colorant"orange" end
function csty(x::Vector{T}) where T<:AbstractRemovalMarker     colorant"tan"    end
function csty(x::Vector{T}) where T<:AbstractSusceptibleMarker colorant"blue"   end 
function csty(x::Vector{T}) where T<:AbstractIncident                           end ;
```

Collect drawing styles including `csty` in the named tuple `style`.
Note that `FigureUtilities` functions frequently
use this _via_ a keyword argument `style` defined there.
```{julia}
style = (
  radius   =  0.2cy,              smradius =  0.9 * 0.2cy,
  bit      = -0.02h,              tic      = -0.2cy,
  xlab     =  0cx-0.4inch,        yloc     = 0.25inch,
  height   =  0.0cy,              
  boundary =  linewidth(1.00mm),  trail    =  linewidth(0.75mm),
  active   =  linewidth(0.75mm),  dormant  =  linewidth(0.25mm),
  blank    =  colorant"white",    scaffold =  colorant"grey",
  region   =  (context(), rectangle(), fill(colorant"bisque"), fillopacity(0.3)),
  colour   =  csty,
) ;
```

# Experiments
Plot regions of infection and removal. First define an epidemic.
```{julia}
env0 = Innovation(5, 
  A[I(0.11,2,3), I(0.2,2,5), P(0.4,1,2), I(0.5,2,5), I(0.6,2,4), I(0.85,3,4), 
    I(0.9,2,3), I(1.0,2,5), P(1.1,2,3), I(1.05,4,5), I(1.2,2,4), I(1.6,3,5), 
    I(1.5,3,4)], 
  R[R(0.3,5), R(0.42,3), R(0.7,3), R(0.55,3), R(0.95,5), R(1.4,2), R(1.55,1),
    R(1.85,2)],
  C[C(1.3,2), C(0.8,1), C(1.7,4), C(1.8,4), C(1.92,5)] ) ;
```


```{julia}
initial= SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0)
chron  = chronology(env0) ; states = [initial] # both will be overwritten
traj, active = evolution_recurse!(states, AbstractIncident[], duration, chron, conditioned=true)

infect1 = [x for x in active if isa(x, I) || isa(x, P)]
infect2 = [(MIA(x.t, x.infectee-1), MIB(x.t, x.infectee)) for x in infect1]
remove1 = [x for x in active if isa(x, C) || isa(x, R)]
remove2 = [(MRA(x.t, k-1), MRB(x.t, k)) for (k, x) in enumerate(remove1)]
active2 = sort(vcat(infect2, remove2), lt=(x,y) -> isearlier(x[1], y[1]))
active_trajectory = collect(Iterators.flatten(active2));
```

Compute indices for initial and continuation markers.

```{julia}
initial0 = [0, 1, population]

initial_markers = Iterators.flatten([
    [IR(0, k) for k in 1:initial0[1]],
    [II(0, k) for k in (initial0[1]+1):(initial0[1]+initial0[2])],
    [IS(0, k) for k in (initial0[1]+initial0[2]+1):population]
  ])

rend = maximum(x.target for x in active_trajectory if isa(x, MRB) )
iend = maximum(x.target for x in active_trajectory if isa(x, MIB))
total_trajectory = collect(Iterators.flatten(
  [ initial_markers, 
    active_trajectory, 
    [CR(duration, k) for k in 1:rend], 
    [CI(duration, k) for k in (rend+1):iend], 
    [CS(duration, k) for k in (iend+1):population]
  ])) ;
```

Here is the total trajectory:
```{julia}
[total_trajectory[1:10], total_trajectory[11:20], total_trajectory[21:end]]
```

## Plotting regions of infection and removal
Note that marker labels omit time-line superscript as this is redundant!
```{julia}
function draw_marker(xl::Vector{T}; sty=style) where T<:AbstractMarker
  if length(xl) > 0
    (context(),
      (context(),
        text(map(x -> (x.t)cx, xl), map(x -> (x.target)cy, xl), 
             map(x -> chop(string(x)), xl), [hcenter], [vcenter]), 
        fontsize(5pt), font("Helvetica")
      ),
      (context(),
        circle(map(x -> (x.t)cx, xl), map(x -> (x.target)cy, xl), [sty.smradius]), 
        fillopacity(0.2), fill(sty.colour(xl)), stroke(sty.colour(xl))
      ), 
      (context(),
        circle(map(x -> (x.t)cx, xl), map(x -> (x.target)cy, xl), [sty.smradius]), 
        fill(sty.blank),
      ),
    )
  end
end ;
```


```{julia}
function infected_areas(population, total_trajectory; sty=style)
  xx= Float64[] ; yy = Integer[] ; rw = Float64[] ; rl = Integer[] ;
  for k in 1:population
    level = [bb for bb in total_trajectory if bb.target==k]
    starts = [bb for bb in level if (isa(bb, MIB) || isa(bb, II))]
    ends   = [bb for bb in level if (isa(bb, MRB) || isa(bb, CI))]
    if length(starts) > 0 && length(ends) > 0
      disk1 = [bb for bb in level if (isa(bb, MIB) || isa(bb, II))][1]
      disk2 = [bb for bb in level if (isa(bb, MRB) || isa(bb, CI))][1]
      append!(xx, disk1.t)
      append!(yy, k-1)
      append!(rw, disk2.t - disk1.t)
      append!(rl, 1)
    end
  end
  return xx, yy, rw, rl
end ;


function removed_areas(population, total_trajectory; sty=style)
  xx= Float64[] ; yy = Integer[] ; rw = Float64[] ; rl = Integer[] ;
  for k in 1:population
    level = [bb for bb in total_trajectory if bb.target==k]
    starts = [bb for bb in level if (isa(bb, MRB) || isa(bb, IR))]
    ends   = [bb for bb in level if (isa(bb, CR))]
    if length(starts) > 0 && length(ends) > 0
      disk1 = starts[1]
      disk2 = ends[1]
      append!(xx, disk1.t)
      append!(yy, k-1)
      append!(rw, disk2.t - disk1.t)
      append!(rl, 1)
    end
  end
  return xx, yy, rw, rl
end ;

xx1, yy1, rw1, rl1 = infected_areas(population, total_trajectory)
xx2, yy2, rw2, rl2 = removed_areas(population, total_trajectory) ;
```

```{julia}
# Epidemic trajectory misses last segment if not continuing. Thus
# append highest MRB if `CI` is not at end.
  
epidemic_trajectory = [(x.t, x.target) for x in total_trajectory 
  if (isa(x, MIA) || isa(x, MIB)  || 
      isa(x, II) || isa(x, CI))]

terminus = epidemic_trajectory[end]
if (terminus[1] < duration)
  end_marker = [x for x in total_trajectory if x.target == terminus[2]][3]
  push!(epidemic_trajectory, (end_marker.t, end_marker.target))
end ;
```

```{julia}
# Removal trajectory may miss last segment. Check, and if so then
# append highest MRB.
removal_trajectory = [(x.t, x.target) for x in total_trajectory 
      if (isa(x, IR) || isa(x, MRA) || isa(x, MRB))]

terminus = removal_trajectory[end]
if (terminus[1] < duration)
  push!(removal_trajectory, (duration, terminus[2]))
end

# should use "total_markers" and ensure "total_trajectory" actually is a trajectory!
Regions = (context(),
  draw_marker([x for x in total_trajectory if isa(x, IS)], sty=style),
  draw_marker([x for x in total_trajectory if isa(x, II)], sty=style),
  draw_marker([x for x in total_trajectory if isa(x, IR)], sty=style),

  draw_marker([x for x in total_trajectory if isa(x, MIA)], sty=style),
  draw_marker([x for x in total_trajectory if isa(x, MIB)], sty=style),

  draw_marker([x for x in total_trajectory if isa(x, MRA)], sty=style),
  draw_marker([x for x in total_trajectory if isa(x, MRB)], sty=style),
  
  draw_marker([x for x in total_trajectory if isa(x, CS)], sty=style),
  draw_marker([x for x in total_trajectory if isa(x, CI)], sty=style),
  draw_marker([x for x in total_trajectory if isa(x, CR)], sty=style),


  (context(),
    rectangle(xx1, yy1, rw1, rl1),
    fill(style.colour(I[])), fillopacity(0.3),
  ),

  (context(),
    rectangle(xx2, yy2, rw2, rl2),
    fill(style.colour(C[])), fillopacity(0.3),
  ),

  (context(),
  line(epidemic_trajectory),
    stroke(style.colour(I[])), style.trail
  ),

  (context(),
    line(removal_trajectory),
     stroke(style.colour(C[])), style.trail
  ),

  scaffolding(duration, population),
  )
depict("Regions", coordinates, Regions)
```

## Plotting removals and conditional removals.
```{julia}
Removals_incidents = (context(),
  draw_incident([inc for inc in env0.removals  if isa(inc, R)], sty=style),
  draw_incident([inc for inc in env0.cremovals if isa(inc, C)], sty=style),
  )
depict("Removals", coordinates, Removals_incidents, Regions)
```

We now need to add linear segments corresponding to "no-infection zones".
```{julia}
timelined_susceptibles = [x for x in total_trajectory if isa(x, IS)]
timelined_removals = [[inc for inc in env0.removals if isa(inc, R)] for k in 1:population]
```

# Computing the last viable epidemic
First establish active removal incidents in time-decreasing order
of _removed_ timeline
(easily done: the \(i^\text{th}\) active removal listed in time-order
will necessarily remove time-line \(i\)),
and list potential infections prior to each active removal
according to infection time.
Notice we have not yet covered the possibility that some time-lines
are never infected and others are not removed before `duration`
(the end of the simulation). Notice too that the first time-line
is (of course) infected at time \(0\) and is not otherwise infected.

```{julia}
active_removals = filter(x -> (isa(x, R) || isa(x, C)), active)
reversed_removals = reverse(collect(enumerate(active_removals))[2:end])
barrier = reversed_removals[1][2]
last_viable = []
for (k, rem) in reversed_removals
  println("Timeline $k ends at $rem, at time $(rem.t)")
  prior_removals = [pr for pr in env0.removals if pr.target==k && pr.t < rem.t]
  println("  (prior rem) ", join([string(pr) for pr in prior_removals], " "))
  prior_infections = [pf for pf in env0.infections if pf.infectee==k && pf.t < rem.t]
  println("  (prior inf) ", join([string(pf) for pf in prior_infections], " "))
  barrier =
      sort( [pf for pf in prior_infections if pf.t < barrier.t], by=x -> x.t)[end]
  println("  (last viable infection) ", barrier)
  println("\n")
  pushfirst!(last_viable, barrier)
end
println("  (last_viable) ", join([string(pr) for pr in last_viable], " "))
```

By the nature of the simulation, no prior potential infections will infect
a time-line _after_ it has been removed, because by then the `target` time-line
must also have been removed.
